newsitem.title: YUGOSLAVIA: Yugo NBY '97 money policy even tighter - c.banker.
newsitem.headline: Yugo NBY '97 money policy even tighter - c.banker.

text.p: The Yugoslav central bank will resort to even tighter money policy in 1997 to ensure overall economic stability and keep the dinar fixed at 3.3 to the German mark, National Bank of Yugoslavia (NBY) Vice-Governor Ratko Banovica said on Monday.
He said an increase in monetary aggregates will match the gross domestic product (GDP) growth rate of 13 percent.
Banovic insisted the first quarter monetary policy will be even more restrictive than in 1996 to create overall stability.
"NBY will have to create monetary equilibrium during the first quarter of 1997, forming the basis for macroeconomic stability," Banovic told a meeting of businessmen and bankers.
"If M1 money supply stands between 5.2 and 5.3 billion dinars at the end of 1996, it is clear that it will not rise much furhter during the course of 1997," he said.
According to the NBY latest reports, M1 stood at 4.596 billion dinars in September.

The vice-governor said the NBY will stick to currency board mechanism (of base money creation) increasing M1 only by matching hard-currency backing. The dinar rate will remain fixed at its current level of 3.3 to the German mark.
Referring to the recent slide in the dinar black market rate, Banovic said the change did not result from additional monetary expansion. -- Gordana Filipovic, Belgrade newsroom, +381 11 222 4254
